summary: Complete Q1 Proposal review of 122 finished with changes-requested. 122 resolves Q1-RP-004: the revised delta passes the installed OpenSpec strict Change validation. It also closes the empty/partial initial-generation gap by making initial explore and initial propose Core-owned complete sets. However, the proposed completeness rule is limited to the initial propose and does not compare a revise-propose successor effective specs namespace with the current canonical specs namespace. A successor can add a new spec while declaring only proposal: inherited refs still match, the successor terminals, and the generic review-entry check validates only that incomplete effective set. The unbound new canonical spec can therefore be approved. Proposal approval remains blocked until completeness is enforced for every current propose effective set, including revise successors.

blockingFindings.title: A revise-propose successor can introduce an unbound spec and still enter review
blockingFindings.evidence: 122 makes complete namespace comparison explicit only for an initial propose (delta 244-279). For a revise-propose, the effective set is the predecessor set plus only declared tags (delta 401-406); the generic review-entry rule then checks only that effective refs resolve and hash-match (411-414). Sequence: P0 completes with complete specs {A}; R0 reviews P0 as changes-requested; P1=revise-propose declares only proposal and adds canonical specs/B. P1 inherits A, so every declared and inherited ref matches. Because P1 did not declare specs, no rule compares its effective specs set {A} against current namespace {A,B}; P1 can terminal and review-propose can bind P1 without B. The initial-only new-spec scenario (266-272) does not cover this successor sequence, while tasks 3.8/5.12 state the intended complete-namespace guarantee.
blockingFindings.impact: A completed revision can be approved while a canonical Proposal spec has no Core-derived content-hash binding. This recreates the initial-coverage trust gap for the normal revise path and defeats the stated current-effective-set guarantee.
blockingFindings.requiredResolution: Make specs-namespace completeness an invariant of every current propose effective set, not just initial propose. At revise-propose terminal preflight and review entry, compare the effective specs refs exactly with the current canonical specs/** namespace; a namespace change must require the specs tag and Core enumeration, otherwise keep the revise Run pending or reject review binding. Align the design, delta Requirement/scenarios, and tasks. Add a negative fixture P0 -> changes-requested review -> P1(proposal only plus new specs/B) that cannot terminal or enter review, alongside the positive P1 with specs declared and Core-enumerated. Preserve the accepted subset overlay for unchanged namespaces.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Explore source links remain checkout-specific
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: The cited source links use file:///D:/Projects/flowkit absolute paths and cannot resolve in another checkout or platform.
nonBlockingFindings.recommendedResolution: Convert source links to repository-relative Markdown links in a future in-scope edit. This does not block the Proposal finding above.
